default_exit._why: one exit for every family so rules compete on the same footing; the owner will decide the demo stop/take-profit later and this block changes then (a change = a new screen run, its variants counted again)
default_exit._fills: signal at the close of bar t; market order at the open of the 1-minute bar that starts at t's close (+ slippage); every 1-minute bar from the entry minute on: stop first (fills at the stop or the gap open, - slippage), then the target (a limit: needs a trade 1 tick through, fills at the target); time exit at the open of the first minute at or after entry + max_hold_min; flat at the session's flatten time; one position at a time; at most max_entries_per_session entries per session

E-928.title: Confirmed pin bar
E-928.hypothesis: A long-wick rejection bar shows one side absorbed; waiting for the next bar to close beyond the pin's extreme filters out unconfirmed wicks and trades with the trapped side's exit.

E-929.title: Thin-volume wide bar fade
E-929.hypothesis: A wide bar on below-average volume is a move without participation (a sweep of thin liquidity); price tends to give it back.

E-930.title: Close-location persistence
E-930.hypothesis: Several consecutive bars closing near their highs (lows) reveal steady aggressive buying (selling) that keeps absorbing the offer; follow its onset.

E-931.title: Sloped-VWAP touch bounce
E-931.hypothesis: When session VWAP has been rising, institutional buyers benchmarked to it defend it; a touch that closes back above is a low-risk continuation (mirror for falling VWAP).

E-932.title: Rolling-VWAP cross
E-932.hypothesis: A short-window volume-weighted average tracks the recent cost basis of active traders; a decisive close through it flips who is underwater.

E-933.title: Shrinking-range ladder break
E-933.hypothesis: Successively smaller bars show sellers/buyers drying up; the first bar breaking the last bar's extreme in the EMA trend direction resumes the trend.

E-934.title: Volume climax at a range extreme
E-934.hypothesis: A heavy-volume push to a new N-minute extreme that closes back in the opposite half of its range is exhaustion: aggressive orders were absorbed by passive liquidity.

E-935.title: Strong block candle follow
E-935.hypothesis: When a 15/30/60-minute block closes with a body filling most of its range, one side controlled the whole block; the next block tends to start in the same direction.

E-936.title: Late-session heavy-volume break
E-936.hypothesis: Heavy volume breaking the prior bar's extreme near the close comes from position-squaring flows that are price-insensitive and keep pushing into the close.

E-937.title: Close-only channel break on volume
E-937.hypothesis: Using closes (not wicks) ignores spikes; a close beyond all recent closes with above-average volume is an accepted price, not a poke, so it should follow through.
